title: Western Ghats
summary: The Western Ghats are a 1,600 km mountain range along India's west coast, also called the Sahyadri. They formed during Gondwana's break-up, shape the monsoon and feed rivers draining almost 40% of India's land. A biodiversity hotspot with at least 325 globally threatened species, they became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2012.

as_recorded.value: The region was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2012.

where.modern_name: Western Ghats (Sahyadri), west coast of India

importance.justification: A major mountain range and watershed that shapes India's monsoon and hosts exceptional biodiversity, recognised as a World Heritage Site.

sources.title: Western Ghats - UNESCO World Heritage Centre

reviewer_note: The range's formation dates are only given as geological periods, so the year 2012 reflects the UNESCO inscription. Sources differ on area (160,000 km2 in Wikipedia vs around 140,000 km² in UNESCO) and on the Jurassic timing (Late Jurassic/Early Cretaceous vs early Jurassic Gondwana breakup).)
